2609.02453.title: Addressing Trust in AI Systems through Education: A Didactic Perspective
2609.02453.paper_summary: Machine learning (ML) education faces two persistent and connected obstacles: many educational tools present ML as an opaque black box, which leaves learners with a superficial understanding, and this same opacity prevents users from forming the calibrated trust that appropriate reliance on AI systems requires. We present ICE-T, a didactic framework that integrates three mutually reinforcing facets: intermodal transfer grounded in Bruner's enactive, iconic, and symbolic modes of representation, computational thinking operationalized through the Use-Modify-Create progression, and explanatory thinking supported by a process model. Connecting the framework to the empirical literature on algorithm aversion, AI literacy, and mental model formation, and to systematic reviews of the K-12 ML activity landscape, we argue that the three facets supply the cognitive mechanisms that the trust calibration literature identifies as drivers of appropriate reliance: representational richness, graduated process control, and the capacity to contextualize errors. On this basis, we propose that trust calibration be treated as an explicit educational objective, with ICE-T as a principled and scalable means of achieving it.
2609.02453.paper_summary_zh: 機器學習 (ML) 教育面臨兩個持續且相互關聯的障礙：許多教育工具將 ML 呈現為一個不透明的黑箱，這使得學習者只能對其有表面的理解，而這種不透明性也阻礙了用戶形成對 AI 系統所需的適當信任。我們提出了 ICE-T，一個教學框架，整合了三個相互增強的面向：基於 Bruner 的動態、圖示和符號表徵模式的跨模態轉移，通過使用-修改-創建進程操作化的計算思維，以及由過程模型支持的解釋性思維。將該框架與關於算法厭惡、AI 素養和心理模型形成的實證文獻，以及 K-12 ML 活動景觀的系統評估相連接，我們主張這三個面向提供了信任校準文獻所識別的適當依賴驅動因素的認知機制：表徵豐富性、漸進的過程控制以及情境化錯誤的能力。在此基礎上，我們建議將信任校準視為一個明確的教育目標，並以 ICE-T 作為實現該目標的原則性和可擴展的方法。
